# v0.29.0-rc2 — local semantic recall on by default, fuller recall and safer retries

This is the second release candidate for v0.29.0; it follows v0.29.0-rc1 and v0.28.1. **Changes since rc1** are listed first; the rest of these notes cover everything since v0.28.1. Recall returns more exact matches from long messages and counts duplicate copies once. Retried and stopped turns are stored more reliably. Compaction stops redoing work that changed nothing. Local semantic recall is now on by default, and three default-on additions write new data to the store; they are listed first below.

Session-pack recall and entity memory stay off by default. No answer-quality gain is claimed for this release. Three release gates are still open (see **Qualification**).

## Changes since rc1

- **Local semantic recall is on by default.** LCM-X now uses on-device embeddings (fastembed with `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5`) out of the box; nothing leaves the machine. The dependency comes from the companion plugin `hermes-lcm-x-local-embeddings`, which `scripts/install.sh` offers. Until the companion, the model and the index are ready, recall answers from full-text search as before and reports `degraded=true` with the reason. Nothing downloads or backfills during a turn: the model fetch and the one-time catch-up over existing history run in the background. `lcm_doctor` shows model readiness separately from index coverage, and names the exact enable command when the companion is missing. To opt out, set `LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=false`. Explicit provider and model settings, cloud consent, and the missing-model check for cloud providers are unchanged for environment settings and new config objects (one Python-only exception is under **Known issues**) ([#1186](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1186), [PR #1956](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1956)).
- **Local embeddings install as a companion plugin.** The local-embedding dependency (fastembed) now ships in a separate companion plugin, `hermes-lcm-x-local-embeddings`, which the host installs with its own consent prompt. LCM-X itself still has no Python dependencies, so declining or failing that install never disables memory: full-text recall keeps working, and the installer prints the exact command to retry. The installer now also targets the right profile when `HERMES_PROFILE` is set or `HERMES_HOME` points at a profile directory, and refuses a conflicting pair before changing anything ([#1186](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1186), [PR #1940](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1940)).
- **Small hosts adapt instead of timing out.** When local embeddings are on by default and the host has at most 2 effective CPUs (affinity, cgroup quota and host capacity are all checked), recall answers from full-text search right away and reports `degraded=true` with reason `cpu_limited` and the real coverage of each arm. An explicit `LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED` setting, or an explicit provider, keeps full control. Background catch-up still runs ([#1186](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1186), [#1586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1586), [PR #1938](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1938)).
- **Embedding prefixes are rollback-safe.** In rc1, after a rollback to v0.28.1 an older reader could pick up vectors made with a query/document prefix, compare unprefixed queries against them and write unprefixed vectors that survived re-upgrade. Prefixed vectors now use their own task names (`summary+prefix`, `chunk+prefix`), which v0.28.1 ignores. Stores without a prefix are unchanged ([#1942](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1942), [PR #1945](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1945)).
- **Entity memory groundwork (off by default, not exposed yet):** internal links from stored facts' subjects to the right person per sender, with reversible corrections. No tool, turn-path or schema change ([#1862](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1862), [PR #1926](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1926)).
- **Summaries ending with a doubled closer are kept.** Some small summary models end a valid summary with `</lcm-summary>` twice. LCM-X treated the second one as the last line and discarded the summary (logged as `reason=no_content`), so the backlog stayed uncompacted until a retry happened to succeed. A run of identical closers at the very end now counts as one and is logged as `tolerated repeated_closer`. Thanks to the community contributor who found and fixed this ([#1948](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1948), [PR #1949](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1949)).
- **Scanner-clean install payload for the plugin catalog.** Each release tag now also publishes a runtime-only copy of the plugin: its import closure plus `plugin.yaml`, `LICENSE` and the bundled skill, built from the tag's exact commit. It is published as a new commit on the `dist` branch (under `plugin/`), with a manifest attached to the release. Current Hermes scans a plugin's whole tree before install, and this payload passes that scan where the full repository does not. The v0.28.1 payload is published, and a catalog update to it has been proposed upstream ([#1946](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1946), [PR #1958](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1958)).

### Testing improved since rc1
- **Release gauntlet instruments:** the D4 recall-health replacement step is a permanent, CI-collected tool that checks that both attempts used the same instrument and lists which fields it compared ([PR #1954](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1954)); the B4 drained-store coverage check accepts witnessed drained coverage and rejects ambiguous tail matches ([#1900](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1900), [PR #1952](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1952)); the Phase A host check runs in an isolated Hermes home and tells "preparing" from "prepared" ([#1941](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1941), [PR #1950](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1950), [PR #1947](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1947)).
- **Host suite:** fixed dependency and capability fixtures that made the host test suite fail for reasons unrelated to the product ([#1539](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1539), [PR #1951](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1951)).
- **Companion and small-host cells:** decline, noninteractive and profile-targeting installs are tested against exact host pins; the CPU detector is tested on affinity, cgroup v1/v2 and malformed inputs; a v0.28.1 rollback test reproduces the prefix contamination before the fix.

## On by default in this release

- **Local semantic recall** (new in rc2; described under **Changes since rc1**). On LongMemEval-S with a frontier reader (measured on v0.26.1), local semantic recall scored 85.8% against 72.2% without embeddings; this release turns it on for everyone who installs the companion.
- **Sender label on gateway messages.** For gateway turns (Telegram, Discord and similar), LCM-X records the sender's platform user ID, for example `telegram:12345`, on the stored user message. It is an unverified label: it is not used for access control and does not change any stored or delivered text. CLI turns record nothing. Older rows are not filled in. Turn it off with `LCM_SENDER_CAPTURE=0` ([#995](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/995), [PR #1875](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1875)).
- **Compaction pause survives restarts.** When an ordinary compaction pass finishes and changes nothing, LCM-X now records that in the session's metadata (`compaction_no_progress:v1:…`), so a restarted engine also waits the fixed 10 minutes before retrying. Forced, overflow, recovery and survival-ceiling compactions never wait ([#1880](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1880), [PR #1888](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1888)).
- **Recall response fields.** Results can now include `duplicate_store_ids` (other exact copies of a hit) and `time_uncertain: carried` (the stored time may not be when the message was said). Both are described below.
- **One INFO log line per session end.** `LCM attribution phase=session_end …` gives the end reason, row and cursor counts and step timings. It never includes message content. The timings overlap; do not add them up ([#1880](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1880), [PR #1906](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1906)).

Everything else under **Changes** is also on by default with no new setting, unless it is listed under **Optional features**.

## Upgrade

- **Host:** Hermes 0.21.3 or newer is still required (0.21.5 or newer recommended), with Python 3.11 or newer. CI now also runs against the latest upstream Hermes as an advisory check only; that does not make upstream Hermes a supported host ([#1919](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1919), [PR #1921](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1921)).
- **Store:** the schema version stays 5. Two empty columns are added to the messages table (`sender_id`, `sender_source`). v0.28.1 ignores them, and rows it writes leave them empty ([PR #1875](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1875)).
- **Optional entity tables:** only when you set `LCM_ENTITIES_ENABLED=1`. The first start with it on creates six tables (`lcm_entities`, `lcm_entity_aliases`, `lcm_entity_keys`, `lcm_memory_notes`, `lcm_memory_events`, `lcm_memory_host_file_revisions`), three indexes and two triggers that keep the event log append-only, and turns on the `lcm_memory` lookup/list tool. Turning the setting off keeps the tables. v0.28.1 leaves them untouched ([#1862](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1862), [PR #1915](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1915)).
- **Chunk embedding triggers:** whenever local embeddings are on (now the default; opt out with `LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=false`). On the first chunk-store open after upgrade, LCM-X adds three triggers to the existing chunk tables (no new tables) and clears its coverage records once, so the next catch-up does a one-time rescan. After a rollback to v0.28.1 the triggers stay in the database and SQLite keeps running them ([#1748](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1748), [PR #1758](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1758), [PR #1843](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1843)).
- **Local semantic recall turns on at upgrade** unless you set `LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED`. Install the companion when the installer offers it, or recall keeps using full text and `lcm_doctor` says so. On an existing store, the first start begins a one-time background catch-up. On hosts with 2 or fewer effective CPUs, the default skips semantic recall and answers from full text; set `LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=true` explicitly to use it there anyway.
- **Rollback:** target `v0.28.1`. Take a SQLite-safe backup first, and compare ordered raw messages and summary provenance through upgrade, rollback and re-upgrade. Rollback with the sender columns and populated entity tables is covered by automated compatibility tests.
- **Deprecated settings:** `LCM_CACHE_FRIENDLY_CONDENSATION_ENABLED` and `LCM_LARGE_OUTPUT_TRANSCRIPT_GC_ENABLED` still work (off by default) and still warn in `/lcm status`, `lcm_status` and `lcm_doctor`. The v0.28.1 notes said they would be removed in v0.29.0; removal now happens in v0.30.0, and the warning text says so ([#1246](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1246), [PR #1932](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1932)).

## Changes since v0.28.1

### Recall and search

- **Matches deep in long messages:** recall now returns up to its full 25 matches when the match sits deep in a long message, each with an exact quote; before, only the first 8 came back. This covers CJK and emoji text and the fallback search path. Ranking and response limits are unchanged ([#1678](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1678), [#1685](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1685), [PR #1679](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1679), [PR #1703](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1703)).
- **Duplicate hits counted once:** exact stored copies of a message (same session, role, tool call, content and recorded time) count once against recall and grep limits. The best-ranked copy is shown; the others are listed in `duplicate_store_ids`. Copies with no recorded time, or different times, stay separate. Stored rows, raw reads and `lcm_expand` are unchanged ([#1681](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1681), [PR #1683](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1683)).
- **Identifiers and broad searches:** a search for an identifier such as `VALUE_S1586_SHARD000007_0000` matches the exact identifier first and broadens only when nothing matches. Broad searches on large stores, and session and vector loading, do less work. Result order and limits are unchanged; no general speed guarantee is claimed ([#1749](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1749), [PR #1745](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1745), [PR #1750](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1750), [PR #1757](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1757)).
- **Media captions are searchable:** newly stored media placeholders keep a short text preview of the caption. Media bytes are not stored in the preview, and older rows are not filled in ([#1702](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1702), [#1718](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1718), [PR #1710](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1710), [PR #1720](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1720)).

### Retries, stopped turns and restarts

- **Retried tool turns:** when a turn is retried after its tool output was pruned, each new message and tool call/result is stored once, both while running and after a restart. Some cold-restart retry shapes are still open (see **Known issues**) ([#1540](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1540), [PR #1830](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1830)).
- **Compaction records are written atomically:** compaction saves its record of which messages it covered in a single database write, so a crash can no longer leave a half-written record that later drops or duplicates a message ([#1451](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1451), [PR #1882](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1882)).
- **Re-sent messages after a restart:** a user message re-sent in the same position with the same text and a later timestamp is now stored instead of dropped. If the host only re-timestamps a message and nothing else tells it apart from a real resend, it may still be stored twice ([#1511](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1511), [#1328](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1328), [PR #1780](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1780), [PR #1810](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1810)).
- **Failed reads retry:** if a database read fails at session start or during an identity check, the next turn retries instead of skipping messages or storing them twice. Before, an edited earlier message could be skipped for good ([#1317](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1317), [#1353](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1353), [PR #1803](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1803), [PR #1807](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1807)).
- **Re-examined messages follow your rules:** when LCM-X re-examines earlier messages, they go through your ignore patterns and large-output rules again, and only those messages are re-checked ([#1628](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1628), [#1822](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1822), [PR #1816](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1816), [PR #1874](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1874)).
- **Stopped turns are saved right away:** a turn you stop after the assistant or a tool has produced output is saved immediately instead of on the next turn. A turn stopped before any reply, or right after a reset, is still saved on the next turn ([#1623](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1623), [PR #1806](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1806)).
- **Two connections, one session:** binding and finishing a session no longer overwrite another connection's live state, and empty-session cleanup no longer removes an engine running in the same process ([#634](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/634), [#753](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/753), [PR #730](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/730), [PR #762](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/762)).
- **Simultaneous opens:** two engines or a maintenance worker opening the same store at once no longer fail with "index already exists" or "trigger already exists" errors ([#1744](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1744), [#1771](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1771), [PR #1747](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1747), [PR #1778](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1778)).

### Compaction and diagnostics

- **Less redundant work:** below the compaction threshold, LCM-X no longer asks the host to rebuild its prompt only to swap large tool outputs for stubs; the swap waits for the next real compaction. Redaction, quarantine and ignore cleanups still apply immediately ([#1880](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1880), [PR #1887](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1887)). The restart-proof pause is described above.
- **Store-wedge inspector:** a new read-only operator tool, `scripts/store_wedge_inspect.py`, reads a stopped copy of a store and reports why compaction is stuck, or `unknown` when it cannot tell. It never repairs anything. Steps are in `docs/operations/store-wedge-inspect.md`, and the doctor's compaction-progress warning links there ([#1598](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1598), [#1162](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1162), [PR #1737](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1737), [PR #1752](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1752), [PR #1786](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1786)).
- **Duplicate-check diagnostics:** the message-ID observer (shadow mode) also counts conflicts that differ only in whitespace. Matching and stored data are unchanged ([#1787](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1787), [PR #1808](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1808)).

### Dates, evidence and configuration

- **Uncertain times are flagged:** when a message's stored time may not be when it was said (for example after an edit or a resend), recall and the evidence tools (`lcm_evidence_pack`, `lcm_compile_evidence`, `lcm_compute`, `lcm_retrieve`) mark it `time_uncertain: carried`, list rows left out at a date cutoff, and do not compute exact date answers from them. Stored times are unchanged ([#1507](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1507), [#1779](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1779), [PR #1776](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1776), [PR #1794](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1794)).
- **Dates read the same way everywhere:** month names and mixed formats such as `2024/05-03` are read the same for every row. When a quote mixes dates from different events, LCM-X marks the day unknown instead of guessing, so some answers that used to carry a date no longer do. If the store cannot be read, automatic evidence compilation falls back with reason `store_unavailable` instead of an error. Automatic compilation itself stays off by default (`LCM_PREANSWER_EVIDENCE_ENABLED`) ([#1801](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1801), [#1811](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1811), [#1851](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1851), [PR #1804](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1804), [PR #1826](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1826), [PR #1858](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1858)).
- **config.yaml without PyYAML:** when PyYAML is missing (as on current upstream Hermes), LCM-X prefers `ruamel.yaml`, and its last-resort parser now keeps quoted strings and simple lists. `lcm.model_thresholds` values must be numbers: write `model: 0.35`, not a quoted number ([#1916](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1916), [PR #1918](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1918)).

## Optional features — off by default

- **Local (on-device) embeddings** moved out of this list: they are on by default from this release (see **Changes since rc1**); `docs/embeddings-setup.md` covers the companion, model choice and opt-out.
- **Embedding catch-up on large stores:** background catch-up no longer rescans already-embedded messages on every pass, and stays correct when messages arrive mid-run, when the chunking policy changes, or after a rollback. `/lcm status` reports failures per database and shows in-flight work separately. Exact semantic recall over large chunk stores loads only the selected chunks. The large-store gate for turning local embeddings on by default is still open ([#1586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1586), [PR #1746](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1746), [PR #1758](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1758), [PR #1802](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1802), [PR #1821](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1821), [PR #1843](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1843), [PR #1860](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1860), [PR #1873](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1873), [PR #1893](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1893), [PR #1903](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1903)).
- **Session-pack recall** (`LCM_RECALL_DELIVERY_UNIT=session`; default `hits`): delivers the messages around each ranked session in source order, keeping tool calls with their results, and now retries fitting groups it skipped for space ([#1188](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1188), [#1828](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1828), [PR #1695](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1695), [PR #1868](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1868)).
- **Entity memory, read-only** (`LCM_ENTITIES_ENABLED=1`): the `lcm_memory` tool's `lookup` and `list` return cited mentions of a person or thing across sessions, with labelled times. Facts from assertions also need `LCM_ASSERTIONS_ENABLED`. Merge, split, undo and forget are not exposed yet ([#1862](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1862), [PR #1865](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1865), [PR #1915](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1915), [PR #1920](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1920)).
- **Embedding prefixes** (Ollama and OpenAI-compatible providers): add a separate text prefix to queries and to documents, for models that expect one, with `LCM_EMBEDDING_QUERY_PREFIX` / `LCM_EMBEDDING_DOCUMENT_PREFIX` or `lcm.embedding_query_prefix` / `lcm.embedding_document_prefix` in config.yaml (quote values to keep spaces; the environment variable wins). A prefix changes the vector identity, so restart Hermes before a warmup or backfill. Thanks to the community contributor who proposed this ([#1118](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1118), [PR #1911](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1911)).

## Testing improved

- **Real-host CI:** an advisory upstream-Hermes cell and config checks without PyYAML; changed tests must actually run (`tests-ran`), and merge-group CI covers previously unselected tests ([#1919](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1919), [PR #1921](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1921), [PR #1783](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1783), [PR #1784](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1784), [PR #1791](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1791), [PR #1793](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1793)).
- **Message-loss reliability checker:** false failures fixed. These are checker fixes, not new product results. The survival-fit deficits once reported on the oldest pinned host came from a scoring gap; with the corrected scorer both runs on that host pass ([#1799](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1799), [#1879](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1879), [PR #1800](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1800), [PR #1870](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1870), [PR #1892](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1892)).
- **Regression tests with every fix:** each recall, loader and date fix above ships with tests that pin payload, ordering and fallback behaviour. A steady-retry change made during this cycle (PR #1637) was reverted before release because it could drop sibling tool results; a regression test now guards that case ([#1636](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1636), [PR #1884](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1884)). The selected-batch chunk loader gains score-tolerance and archived-exclusion regressions ([#1901](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1901), [PR #1927](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1927)).
- **Upgrade and rollback tests:** the sender columns and the optional entity tables are tested against pinned older releases up to v0.28.1, and compatibility fixtures now use SQLite-safe backups that include WAL data ([#1909](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1909), [PR #1913](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1913), [PR #1792](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1792), [PR #1768](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1768)).
- **Flaky tests made deterministic:** timing-sensitive tests now use explicit barriers, drains and logical clocks, and passing tests no longer keep their temporary stores ([#1923](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1923), [#1905](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1905), [PR #1925](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1925), [PR #1930](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1930), [PR #1690](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1690), [PR #1717](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1717), [PR #1835](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1835), [PR #1856](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1856)).
- **Measurement tools:** new probes for local embedding catch-up (speed, CPU, recall while catching up, integrity); the Frontier Measurement Protocol harness gains strict verdict parsing, paired run checks and speaker-label and session-date variants; release-gate comparison rules (D1/D4/D8) and the calibrated Track S rule get producers, scorers and bounded retries ([#1586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1586), [#1189](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1189), [#1824](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1824), [PR #1751](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1751), [PR #1849](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1849), [PR #1866](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1866), [PR #1861](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1861)).
- **Public results:** the results page, README highlights and plugin description now come from one sourced dataset with drift checks, each new scoreboard row is its own file, and the pending check rejects duplicate row IDs and supersession cycles ([#1885](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1885), [#1895](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1895), [PR #1928](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1928), [PR #1857](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1857), [PR #1886](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1886)).

## Known issues

- **Catalog install on upstream Hermes with the plugin scanner:** the catalog entry still pins the full repository, which current Hermes rates `dangerous` and refuses to install. A catalog update to the scanner-clean payload is proposed upstream; until it lands, use `scripts/install.sh` on those hosts. This release's payload is rated `caution` (not `safe`) because the small-host CPU detector reads `/proc`; nothing was changed to hide that from the scanner, and an upstream allowance is requested ([#1946](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1946)).
- **Upstream Hermes manual `/compress`:** on current upstream Hermes main, a manual `/compress` from the gateway uses the host's own compressor and bypasses LCM-X, so stored history can gain duplicate replies. No rows were lost in the reported cases. A fix is proposed upstream ([Hermes #143587](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/143587)); an LCM-X defence is planned for v0.30.0 ([#1922](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1922), [#1924](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1924)).
- **Retry shapes still being fixed** (all are redesigned together for v0.30.0, including the two cases that can lose a row, #1837 and #1838):
  - after a tool call is retried with new message IDs, each later cold restart can store that call and its result again: one more copy per restart, nothing lost ([#1836](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1836));
  - after a cold restart, if only the tool result's message ID changes on a retry, the new result may not be stored ([#1837](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1837));
  - if the plugin restarts before a session's first compaction and the host re-sends the last tool turn with a new timestamp, that turn may not be stored ([#1838](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1838));
  - in some retry and restart sequences after compaction, a replaced or retried message can be dropped or stored twice ([#1451](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1451)).
  Real-host frequency is unknown.
- **Crash before a reply, then rotation:** on hosts that do not give messages unique IDs, if the agent crashes before replying and the conversation then rotates, the next turn can be stored twice. The v0.28.1 notes planned this fix for v0.29.0; it now targets v0.30.0 ([#1508](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1508)).
- **Duplicates kept on purpose:** turns stored before this release's carried-stamp marker can be stored again by a replay, and user messages that the host itself mirrors after an ACP crash recovery are kept twice. LCM-X keeps both copies rather than risk losing a genuine message; see `docs/identity-ledger.md` ([#1501](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1501), [PR #1775](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1775)).
- **Local embeddings on large, fully embedded stores (small hosts):** on a 2-CPU host with a 250,000-row fully embedded store, a semantic recall could use its full 8-second budget. Since rc2, hosts with at most 2 effective CPUs answer from full text immediately when local embeddings are on by default (`degraded=true`, `cpu_limited`); explicit settings keep control. Faster exact semantic recall under contention is planned for v0.29.1 ([#1586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1586), [PR #1939](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1939)).
- **Python only: switching an existing config object to a cloud provider:** if code changes `embedding_provider` to a cloud provider on an `LCMConfig` that already resolved to the local default (with `dataclasses.replace` or attribute assignment), the enabled setting carries over, and that provider starts receiving text without `embeddings_enabled=True`. Settings from the environment and new `LCMConfig(...)` objects are not affected. Set `embeddings_enabled` explicitly when you switch providers in code; a fix is tracked in [#1959](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1959).
- **Subagent work is not stored:** what a delegated subagent does in its own session, including its tool calls and intermediate results, is not stored by LCM-X. Only what the subagent returns to the parent conversation is stored, so `lcm_recall` cannot find a subagent's intermediate results. This isolation is not new in this release. Storing subagent sessions is planned for v0.30.0 ([#1931](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1931)).
- **Cross-process cleanup:** another process sharing the store can still clear an empty live session binding and stall later compaction ([#753](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/753), [#761](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/761)).
- **Extra rows in one degraded mode:** when a child compaction can never publish, three runtime hosts store extra rows and repeat user tags. No user content is missing. That reliability cell now gates on missing content only ([#1797](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1797), [#1900](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1900), [PR #1929](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1929)).

## Qualification

This is a release candidate for testing. It is not qualified for general use yet, and v0.28.1 remains the latest stable release. GA needs every gate below, run on this candidate. Because local semantic recall is now the default, the recall gates (D1, D4 and D8) run on it, with embeddings off recorded beside it; a LongMemEval-S preference no-loss row is recorded in this release and gates from the next minor.

- Small-host local embeddings ([#1586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1586)): catch-up coverage and CPU **PASS**; recall on a large, fully embedded store **FAIL** (see **Known issues**). The local-embedding default does not change. Before GA, that recall is compared with v0.28.1 on the same store, and a slowdown blocks GA: **TBD**.
- Sender and event time ([#995](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/995)): held-out check **PASS** with two judges; agentic tool-loop check: **TBD**.
- Full suite, the CI way, at the rc base: **TBD**.
- Reliability matrix on the release candidate, gating on missing content ([#1900](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1900)): **TBD**.
- Track S facts kept, paired per fact against v0.28.1: **TBD**.
- Recall scorecard fast tier: zero unexplained per-question changes against v0.28.1: **TBD**.
- Reference-agent soak: **TBD**.
- Retry fixes for [#1837](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1837) and [#1838](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1838): moved to the v0.30.0 occurrence redesign; they do not gate v0.29.0.
